claim_verdicts.evidence: ProductCache.cs:13-14 verbatim: `public sealed class ProductCache(IProductRepository inner, IConnectionMultiplexer redis, ILogger<ProductCache> logger)` / `: IProductRepository`. The base list holds only the interface, so no base class is declared (round-1 wording fixed to "declares no base class"; refs inheritance.md:27 on System.Object no longer contradicted).

ProductCache.cs:28-29 `var cached = await GetAsync(key); if (cached is not null) return cached; // cache hit: no query` (inner not called); :41-43 `var product = await inner.FindAsync(id); if (product is not null) await SetAsync(key, product); return product;`. Lesson s4 hit sentence and "when no product has that id, it stores nothing" match. ProductCache.cs names EfProductRepository only in the comment at :11.
ProductCache.cs:56-58: `var product = await inner.UpdatePriceAsync(id, priceVnd); if (product is not null) await RemoveAsync($"product:{id}"); return product;`

EfProductRepository.cs:7 `public sealed class EfProductRepository(DonHangDbContext db) : IProductRepository`; :9 `public async Task<Product?> FindAsync(int id) => await db.Products.FindAsync(id);`. File has 20 lines, no `using StackExchange.Redis`, no Redis identifier.

refs interface.md:12: "Any class, record, or struct that implements that contract must provide an implementation of the members defined in the interface." (Default interface members are an exception, :49; IProductRepository.cs at stage-2 declares only FindAsync and UpdatePriceAsync, both without bodies, so the lesson's conclusion holds.)
refs sealed.md:13: "When you apply the `sealed` modifier to a class, it prevents other classes from inheriting from that class." EfProductRepository.cs:7 is `public sealed class`.

refs DI :279 "Registering a service with only an implementation type is equivalent to registering the service with the same implementation and service type". guidelines.md:198: overloads "accept a Func<IServiceProvider, T>". overview.md:81 "Services can be resolved using IServiceProvider (the built-in service container)". Blazor DI :374 services "resolved using ... GetRequiredService". Only IProductRepository registration at stage-2 is the factory (git grep), so none gets it bare.

ProductsController.cs:15 `(DonHangDbContext db, IProductRepository products)`; :54 `products.FindAsync(id)` in Get; :63-67 `[Authorize(Policy = "StaffOnly")] [HttpPatch(...)]` ... `products.UpdatePriceAsync(id, request.PriceVnd)`; :29 List uses `IQueryable<Product> query = db.Products;`.

git grep on stage-2: `IProductRepository -- DonHang.Api` -> ProductsController.cs:12 (comment) and :15 (`ProductsController(DonHangDbContext db, IProductRepository products)`); `new ProductCache -- *.cs` -> one line `DonHang.Infrastructure/ServiceCollectionExtensions.cs:44:        services.AddScoped<IProductRepository>(provider => new ProductCache(`. Matches new s7 text. Controller code has no ProductCache/EfProductRepository identifier outside comments.

Type-level check of the code: ProductCache.cs:13 takes `IProductRepository inner` and :14 implements `IProductRepository`, so any IProductRepository (including a ProductCache) can be passed as inner; ProductsController.cs:15 depends only on IProductRepository. The timing wrapper is hypothetical and stated as 'could'.

Design reasoning, not a factual claim about a tool; conditioned in the lesson by the observable symptom ('a change to how long copies live means editing the class that holds the queries'). Consistent with the code: TTL lives in ProductCache.cs:18, not in EfProductRepository.cs.

Design reasoning following from claim 11 (inner typed as the interface) and claim 7 (sealed prevents inheriting). Stated in the lesson with a concrete symptom (second implementation needs a second subclass), not as an absolute.
